gpt_5_mini/001:
The strategy for this policy:
- Generate all legal captures (multi-jumps) first — captures are mandatory. For each piece, recursively search capture sequences, stopping if a man reaches promotion row (crowning ends the jump in this implementation, which is standard in many rulesets).
- Score capture sequences by (1) number of pieces captured (primary), (2) whether the sequence yields promotion, (3) safety of the final landing square (avoid immediate recapture), and (4) centrality to prefer safer/stronger positions.
- If no captures exist, generate all simple moves and pick one that promotes, avoids immediate recapture, and moves toward the center.
- Men move forward (white up/increasing row, black down/decreasing row). Men capture forward in this policy (consistent with a common checkers rule set), kings capture in all four diagonal directions.
- The policy always returns a legal move (start and final square). It's designed to be greedy but capture-aware and to avoid moving into obvious immediate recaptures where possible.

The strategy for this policy:

- Generate all legal moves, respecting mandatory captures and multi-jump sequences.
- Use a minimax search with alpha-beta pruning to choose the move that maximizes a static evaluation of the resulting position. The evaluation values kings higher than men and favors advanced men (closer to promotion). Mobility (number of moves) is a small tie-breaker.
- During capture generation the policy explores multi-jump sequences correctly and handles promotion (promotion ends a jump sequence).
- The search respects a short time budget to ensure it returns quickly and always produces a legal move.

The implementation below returns a single move as ((from_row, from_col), (to_row, to_col)). It always returns one of the legal moves (captures if any exist), and uses the minimax result to pick the best available move.
gpt_5_mini/003:
Strategy summary:
- Mandatory captures are enforced and multi-jumps are supported.
- The policy generates all legal captures first; if none exist it considers quiet moves.
- It uses a depth-limited alpha-beta search with a material-plus-position heuristic (men and kings weighted, advancement/promotion bonuses, mobility) and simple move ordering (prefer captures, promotions, multi-captures).
- Search depth is adaptive: deeper search when few pieces remain to allow stronger endgame play while staying fast.
- Men are treated as forward-moving only (no backward non-king moves); promotion ends a capturing sequence (standard English/American draughts convention).
- The policy always returns a legal move.

- Generate all possible capture sequences (including multi-jumps) and prefer moves that capture the most enemy pieces.
- Break ties using a lightweight one-ply evaluation: material (men and kings), promotion potential, piece advancement, and avoids moves that immediately allow the opponent a strong reply (especially immediate captures).
- If no captures exist, choose a safe and advancing non-capturing move using the same heuristic.
- The implementation uses a precise move generator for men (forward moves/captures) and kings (both directions), simulates resulting boards, and picks the best move according to the heuristic.
